# lumos_integration_connection_schema (Data Source)

The credentials and settings an integration takes when connected with `lumos_app`, as JSON Schema documents.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The auth and settings keys an integration takes when connected with
# lumos_app. Both are JSON Schema documents, as JSON strings.
data "lumos_integration_connection_schema" "okta" {
  app_class_id = "okta.com"
}

output "okta_credential_keys" {
  value = keys(jsondecode(data.lumos_integration_connection_schema.okta.auth_schema).properties)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_class_id` (String) Canonical identifier of the integration the schema is for (echoes the request).

### Read-Only

- `auth_schema` (String) JSON Schema describing the auth object lumos_app takes for this integration. Its properties are the credential keys the integration accepts; secret fields are marked writeOnly, and fixed-choice fields carry an enum. Some integrations nest credentials under named groups when they support several authentication methods. An object schema with no properties means no credentials are supplied up front: the connection is completed through browser consent in the Lumos UI. Parsed as JSON.
- `settings_schema` (String) JSON Schema of the non-secret `settings` object for the Apps API's create endpoint. Carries tenant URLs, routing configuration, and other non-secret values the integration needs beyond credentials. Some integrations require a manually-set instance id as `app_instance_identifier` (e.g. an Okta domain); others derive it from the credentials during connect. Integrations that run through an on-prem agent take `on_prem_agent_cluster_id` here. Integrations that need no non-secret configuration return an empty object. Parsed as JSON.
